minutes.headline: Finance Committee previewed FY23 needs with library and land use directors and flagged IT strategy and bus contract
minutes.summary: The committee held informal budget previews with the library director (by Zoom) and the land use director, then covered the Special Town Meeting timeline, technology planning after the IT director's resignation, and TCP building articles. Committee reports raised the school bus contract renewal option. Only adjournment was voted.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town applied for an insurance-carrier risk management grant to move email and platform to Microsoft Office 365.
Town plans to apply for the grant for IT equipment upgrades, due October 1.
Council on aging applied for a community enrichment grant to make the patio ADA compliant.
State closed out with a surplus; MMA asked to add money to Chapter 90 in the supplemental bill.
Governor proposed a short-term plan from state ARPA funds that could affect the town's own ARPA plan.
E-book spending rose and usage roughly doubled over two years; licenses cost far more than discounted print books.
Staff costs are the bulk of the library budget; expanded hours are likely.
Overdue fee revenue had nearly disappeared; trustees want to remove overdue fees.
Remaining capital funds from the original article, after the population study; a further capital article may come.
Assessors propose raising the elderly abatement for single and married persons.
Third year of a three-year bus contract; the renewal option carries a substantial increase and re-bidding is being considered.

decisions.decision: Joint meeting with the School Committee set for October 28 with a MASC speaker on Chapter 70.
Public hearing on the Special Town Meeting set for October 14; town manager to circulate a draft warrant.
September 23 meeting will host the superintendent and town manager; no meeting planned September 30.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee held informal FY23 budget previews with the library director and the land use director; no votes were taken, only adjournment.
The library director described rising e-book costs, doubled usage and no longer needing overdue fees, which trustees want to remove.
The committee heard that the school bus contract is in its third year and the renewal option carries a substantial increase, with re-bidding under consideration.
The Special Town Meeting public hearing was set for October 14, with the town manager to circulate a draft warrant.
Technology planning and cybersecurity were discussed with no resolution, following the IT director's resignation.

why_it_matters: The bus contract renewal option, the library's shift to costly e-book licenses and the loss of overdue-fee revenue are all pressures that may reach the FY23 budget, and so possibly the tax bill.
The Special Town Meeting warrant and the October 28 joint meeting on Chapter 70 are where residents may be asked to vote or hear how state school aid is expected to shape the budget.
watch_next: Public hearing on the Special Town Meeting on October 14, with the draft warrant from the town manager.
September 23 meeting with the superintendent and town manager, and the October 28 joint meeting with the School Committee on Chapter 70.
